💡 This review uniquely bridges ML with liquid electrolyte science, offering tailored workflows for dataset construction and feature representation. It systematically examines ML strategies for ionic transport, electrochemical windows, interphase regulation, and multi-objective optimization, while addressing data quality, generalizability, and interpretability. Its significance lies in guiding mechanism-informed, transferable ML frameworks for rational electrolyte design and accelerated battery development.

💡 This review uniquely consolidates additive-assisted zinc−air hybrid batteries that couple anodic additive oxidation with oxygen reduction for concurrent energy storage and chemical upgrading. It provides actionable guidance for rational design and practical deployment of next-generation energy-saving devices.

item.title: Site‐Selectively Engineered MoS 2 /ReS 2 Heterostructures for High‐Performance Supercapacitors
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in selective Fe doping of only the MoS2 domain within MoS2/ReS2 heterostructures, creating an interfacial built-in electric field that enhances electron/ion transport, strengthens Mo─S bonds, and suppresses Mo dissolution. This yields high capacitance, 97.0% retention over 5000 cycles, and 55.2 Wh kg−1 energy density, offering a design strategy for advanced supercapacitors.

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in identifying ligand electronics and metal-site acidity as molecular descriptors for high-voltage-stable MOF electrolytes, guiding the design of perfluorinated Al-FBDC with a 4.82 V oxidation onset. Its incorporation into composite cathodes suppresses parasitic reactions, enabling Li||Al-FBDC@NCM quasi-solid-state cells with 82% capacity retention over 200 cycles at 4.5 V. This offers a general design principle for high-energy-density lithium-metal batteries.
🏷 lithium-metal battery · MOF electrolyte · high voltage · quasi-solid-state · ligand electronics

item.description:

💡 Trace Al doping into Mn-rich NASICON cathode stabilizes the lattice and modulates MnO6 electronic structure, markedly suppressing voltage hysteresis while preserving the two-phase mechanism. This activates Mn redox couples and lowers Na-ion migration barriers, yielding 138 mAh g−1, 419 Wh kg−1, and 90% capacity retention over 100 cycles—demonstrating a simple, effective strategy for high-performance sodium-ion batteries.
